notes: Read-only run against W at f14dbc1d. I created only the probe folder /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/L11b_v/ with probe.jl and out.txt (the probe's output; the bracketed tags cited above are its lines). The probe ran three times: the first run failed on a Logging import, the second on an unqualified StopPolicy, the third ran clean. One rule applied throughout: when an annotation in the same log entry states the current code fact, I judged the claim conforming and named the annotation line. When the claim is stale and only a later entry or a commit records the change, I judged it drift. Many drift items are pure renames (001-016). log_rules.md rule 2 says entries keep the vocabulary of their day, so for those the right remedy may be an annotation or nothing. I marked them clear=false for that reason. Two real deviations: 093 (EmptyGreedyClaim names its own writer, against D-228, while spec Appendix C agrees with the code) and 170 (incumbent_status returns the harness record for an unclaimed root input; the log and spec.md:9484 say nothing). Open: 101 counts allocations on Julia 1.13.3, where one Vector is two allocations. 156 holds for frame throws, but since D-317 a fault outside the frame ends stopped.
